# 1 Samuel Chapter 18 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 180v-181r | **Source Image:** 1SA_018_page_001.jpg, 1SA_018_page_002.jpg

---

**1** When David had finished speaking with Saul, the soul of Jonathan was bound to the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as he loved his own life.

**2** From that day Saul kept David with him and did not let him return to his father's house.

**3** Jonathan made a covenant with David, because he loved him as he loved his own life.

**4** Jonathan took off the robe he was wearing and gave it to David, along with his tunic, his sword, his bow, and his belt.

**5** David went out and was successful wherever Saul sent him. Saul set him over the fighting men, and this was pleasing in the eyes of all the people and in the eyes of Saul's officials as well.

**6** When the troops returned, as David was coming back from striking down the Philistine, the women came out from all the towns of Israel, singing and dancing, to meet King Saul with tambourines, shouts of joy, and three-stringed instruments.

**7** As they danced, the women sang to one another: "Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his tens of thousands."

**8** Saul was furious, and this refrain galled him. He said, "They have credited David with tens of thousands, but me with only thousands. What more can he get but the kingdom?"

**9** From that day on, Saul kept a jealous eye on David.

**10** The next day a tormenting spirit from God rushed upon Saul, and he raved inside the house while David was playing the lyre as usual. Saul had a spear in his hand,

**11** and he hurled the spear, thinking, "I will pin David to the wall." But David eluded him twice.

**12** Saul was afraid of David, because the LORD was with David but had departed from Saul.

**13** So Saul removed David from his presence and made him a commander of a thousand. David led the troops in their campaigns.

**14** In everything he did, David had great success, because the LORD was with him.

**15** When Saul saw how successful David was, he was filled with dread.

**16** But all Israel and Judah loved David, because he led them in their campaigns.

**17** Saul said to David, "Here is my older daughter Merab. I will give her to you in marriage. Only serve me bravely and fight the LORD's battles." For Saul thought, "I will not raise my hand against him. Let the Philistines do it."

**18** David said to Saul, "Who am I, and what is my family or my father's clan in Israel, that I should become the king's son-in-law?"

**19** But when the time came for Merab, Saul's daughter, to be given to David, she was given in marriage to Adriel of Meholah instead.

**20** Now Saul's daughter Michal was in love with David. When they told Saul, the thing pleased him.

**21** Saul thought, "I will give her to him so that she may be a snare to him and the hand of the Philistines may be against him." So Saul said to David a second time, "You shall now become my son-in-law."

**22** Saul commanded his servants, "Speak to David privately and tell him, 'Look, the king is pleased with you, and all his servants love you. Now become the king's son-in-law.'"

**23** Saul's servants repeated these words to David. But David said, "Does it seem to you a small matter to become the king's son-in-law? I am a poor man and of no standing."

**24** When Saul's servants reported David's words back to him,

**25** Saul said, "Say this to David: 'The king desires no bride-price except a hundred Philistine foreskins, to take vengeance on the king's enemies.'" Saul's plan was to have David fall by the hand of the Philistines.

**26** When the servants told David these terms, it pleased David to become the king's son-in-law. Before the allotted time had passed,

**27** David went out with his men and killed two hundred Philistines. He brought their foreskins and presented them in full count to the king so that he might become the king's son-in-law. Then Saul gave him his daughter Michal in marriage.

**28** When Saul realized that the LORD was with David and that his daughter Michal loved him,

**29** Saul became even more afraid of David. So Saul was David's enemy for the rest of his days.

**30** The Philistine commanders continued to go out to battle, and as often as they did, David had more success than all of Saul's other officers. His name became highly esteemed.

---

## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **18:1 — "The soul of Jonathan was bound to the soul of David"**: The Hebrew *niqsh'rah* (נִקְשְׁרָה) means "was tied, bound, knotted." The *nephesh* (soul/life/self) of Jonathan was literally fastened to David's. This is covenant language of the deepest kind — not sentiment but a binding of destinies. Jonathan's subsequent gift of robe, weapons, and belt (v. 4) constitutes a symbolic transfer of royal succession rights, since Jonathan was the crown prince.

- **18:4 — The robe and weapons**: Jonathan strips himself of every symbol of royal identity — his *me'il* (robe of office), his sword, his bow, his belt. This is not merely friendship but political theology: the heir to Saul's throne voluntarily defers to God's chosen king. Jonathan enacts in private what will only become public knowledge much later.

- **18:7 — "Saul his thousands, David his tens of thousands"**: The women's antiphonal song uses standard Hebrew poetic parallelism (ascending numbers), which need not imply literal comparison. But Saul hears it as a political threat. The Hebrew *va-yichar* (וַיִּחַר — "it burned") reveals that Saul's anger is visceral, not calculated. The seed of murderous jealousy is planted in a celebratory song.

- **18:10 — "A tormenting spirit from God"**: The Hebrew *ruach elohim ra'ah* (רוּחַ אֱלֹהִים רָעָה) is theologically provocative — the text attributes this spirit's origin to God. The narrator does not soften or explain this. The same God who sent his Spirit upon David (16:13) sends a dark spirit upon Saul. The biblical theology of divine sovereignty encompasses both empowerment and judgment.

- **18:25 — "A hundred Philistine foreskins"**: The bride-price (*mohar*) Saul demands is designed as a death sentence disguised as a military honor. Foreskins serve as proof of Philistine kills (since Israelites were circumcised). David's doubling of the requirement (200 instead of 100) demonstrates both his military prowess and his eagerness — and frustrates Saul's trap entirely.

— *PNEUMA*
